PEOPLE

Taehee Kim 김태희

ASSISTANT PROFESSOR · PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATOR

Taehee Kim is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Materials Science and Engineering at Dankook University and leads DMSE Lab. The lab's research spans sol–gel synthesis of nanoporous aerogels, electrocatalysis for hydrogen and oxygen evolution and ammonia oxidation, electrified CO₂ capture, and machine-learning-driven materials design.

Before joining Dankook in September 2026, Kim was a Research Professor (Sejong Science Fellow) at the Aerogel Materials Research Center of Yonsei University and a postdoctoral visiting scholar in the group of Prof. Ted Sargent at Northwestern University. Kim received a joint M.Sc.–Ph.D. in Materials Science and Engineering from Yonsei University, advised by Prof. Sang-Woo Kim and Prof. Hyung-Ho Park, and a B.Sc. (Hons) in Chemistry from the University of Edinburgh.

RESEARCH INTERESTS

What keeps us busy.

  • Sol–gel synthesis of nanoporous metal oxides, metals and metal sulfides by aerogel, hydrothermal and solvothermal routes
  • High-surface-area porous electrodes and supports for electrochemical energy conversion
  • Electrocatalytic water splitting on noble and non-noble metals, mixed oxides and layered double hydroxides
  • Electrochemical ammonia oxidation for direct ammonia fuel cells and nitrogen remediation
  • Plasma-assisted electrochemistry: direct methane partial oxidation and NOₓ reduction
  • Cation effects on electrified CO₂ capture and release with MnO₂
  • Foundation machine-learning interatomic potentials for zero-shot screening of electrocatalyst surfaces
  • Potential-resolved microkinetic modelling and selectivity mapping
  • Large-language-model literature mining and data-driven activity prediction for catalyst discovery
  • Aerogel-based thermal insulation and transparent windows
